rationale: The attestations from Beowulf (B. 766) and the Exeter Book suggest physical movement or progression, which aligns best with travel.v.01 ("change location; move, travel, or proceed"). The Old English verb a-teáh (from tēon, "to draw/go") in these poetic contexts typically refers to moving or proceeding through space, making the basic locomotion sense the best fit among the candidates.
